items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: When Shadow left, we got Jo Jones... But working with him was an experience in another way... Of course, after Jo left... I think Jo stayed there until I left

ctx.x: No, it wasn't Cecil Payne. Anyway, Jo Jones had been working with Illinois, and Jo left for some reason, and I think Shadow Wilson was supposed to have come back with the band. As a matter of fact, I think Shadow did come back and worked a week or so with him. Then we went to Providence, Rhode Island, and it seems as if, at the time we left New York, Shadow couldn't be found anywhere, and we had to leave without him. In the meantime, Illinois is frantic to have a drummer, and he asked me about a drummer. So I…

So we sent and got Dude Brown, and Dude Brown came into Providence. And the rest is history, because I think since then, Illinois has probably used Dude Brown more than any other drummer, here and in Europe and a lot of other places.

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: Tommy Potter and all the guys, John Malachi, all of the guys were going down to the Crystal Cavern. I'd go down there and hang around with them

ctx.x: You see, the thing of it is I had to go to Washington. I knew a little drummer by the name of Cees. So Tommy Potter and all the guys, John Malachi, all of the guys were going down to the Crystal Cavern. I'd go down there and hang around with them and sit down in a little restaurant, sit down and talk about things to come. I'd say, "Now you're going to grow up and when you come to New York, look me up. Go around and hang out with so-and-so and learn," because they had a couple of drummers around there, just doing…
